clue.text: Criticism for each returned fish

indicators.note: returned means the word for each is sent back the way it came, read right to left

parts.note: per means each, as in a pound per person
the roach is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Someone complains about the fish they each sent back to the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is only a link word; 'each' alone supplies the Latin-derived per.
explanation.definitionFit: A reproach is a rebuke or expression of disapproval, a form of criticism.

clue.text: Block is in place

indicators.note: in tells us the little word is goes inside the word for place

parts.note: to rest something is to place or set it down

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a block or barrier is already installed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Block' and 'place' both look like nouns; here both are verbs.
explanation.definitionFit: To block an attack or change is to resist it, as verbs of opposing.

clue.text: First and foremost, one student is behind most of school year

indicators.note: the one-student pair sits behind most of the school word, just before its final year letter

parts.note: a primary school year, with Y the abbreviation for year at its end
one is the Roman numeral I
L is a learner driver, the usual student

explanation.surface: A pupil is kept down, lagging behind for most of the school year.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as the setter wrote it: most of 'school', then one and student, then the year letter; the same letters result. L is the learner plate on British cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Primarily is an adverb meaning chiefly or above all, the same idea as first and foremost.

clue.text: Busy during month, e.g. October

indicators.note: during says the letters lie within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Someone is busy in an autumn month like October.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of 'month' through 'e.g.' into 'October'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the go is an idiom for being constantly active and busy.

clue.text: Mate finishes this chapter — he's succeeded

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in family trees

explanation.surface: A friend completes this chapter of a book, having made it through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mate' looks like a friend, but here it is checkmate.
explanation.definitionFit: Checkmate is the move that ends a game of this board game, so it is what mate finishes.

clue.text: Charm from a drug smuggler ending in airport

parts.note: a mule is someone paid to carry drugs across a border

indicators.note: ending in picks the final letter of the word airport

explanation.surface: A lucky charm is taken from a drug courier at the end of his trip through an airport.
explanation.definitionFit: An amulet is a charm worn to ward off evil, a talisman.

clue.text: Doctor is calm about uranium? Pleasing to hear

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the uranium symbol
to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters of is calm are rearranged

parts.note: U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A physician stays unruffled about a radioactive element.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' rearranges IS CALM to MSICAL; 'about' wraps it round U after the M.
explanation.definitionFit: Something musical is melodious, agreeable to the ear.

clue.text: Pants initially large — one usually selects Y-fronts

definitions.note: pants is British slang for rubbish or very poor, an adjective here

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Large underpants: a shopper's habit of choosing Y-fronts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' looks like underwear but is British slang for awful. Y-fronts are British men's briefs.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang both words mean dreadful or of poor quality.

clue.text: Turn over and seize the woman at the same time

parts.note: TO is the abbreviation for turn over, written at the foot of a page
to get something can mean to seize or catch it
her is the pronoun for the woman

explanation.surface: Instructions to flip something and grab a woman, all at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn over' suggests a reversal, but it is simply the abbreviation TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing things together means doing them simultaneously, in the same moment.

clue.text: Show welcoming resistance with Boris's last U-turn

indicators.note: welcoming means the word for show takes in other letters

parts.note: to reveal is to show
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

indicators.note: last picks the final letter of Boris's

explanation.surface: A display welcoming opposition to a politician's latest change of policy.
explanation.definitionFit: A reversal is a complete change of direction or policy, which a U-turn is.

clue.text: Meandering bus trip gets near city

indicators.note: meandering means wandering about, so the letters of the phrase wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A rambling coach tour brings travellers close to a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meandering' rearranges BUS TRIP GETS NEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Russian port city on the Neva, once the imperial capital.

clue.text: Marine mammals, perhaps captured — one hopefully has them on board

definitions.text: one hopefully has them on board

indicators.note: captured means the abbreviation for perhaps is held inside the mammals

parts.note: seals are mammals living in the sea
EG, for example, signals perhaps

explanation.surface: Sea creatures, maybe caught; a sailor hopes to have them aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' gives EG because an example is only one possibility.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the knack of keeping balance on a moving ship is what a sailor hopes to have when aboard.

clue.text: Put information into code in French vault

parts.note: en is French for in
a crypt is an underground vault in a church

explanation.surface: Someone encodes data in French, in a vault.
explanation.definitionFit: To encrypt data is to convert it into a cipher so it cannot be read.

clue.text: Cooked our moist chicken

indicators.note: cooked means prepared or fiddled, so the letters of our moist are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone has prepared a juicy chicken dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chicken' looks like the food; it is the adjective for cowardly.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicken as slang for cowardly matches timorous, meaning nervous and easily frightened.

clue.text: Alder — one exotic shrub

indicators.note: exotic means outlandish or strange, so the letters are put into an unfamiliar order

explanation.surface: An alder tree is one unusual bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exotic' rearranges ALDER and ONE together.
explanation.definitionFit: The oleander is a poisonous evergreen shrub with pink or white flowers.

clue.text: John's energy unrestricted

parts.note: a john is slang for a toilet, as is loo, so john's gives loo's
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A man named John has boundless vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: John looks like a name but is slang for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose means free from restraint, not tied up or confined.

clue.text: I have to support Aida, say — tense worker

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting letters sit underneath the others

parts.note: Aida is an opera by Verdi
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: A performer backs a Verdi production, a nervous member of the crew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tense' looks like nervous but is the grammar abbreviation T.
explanation.definitionFit: An operative is a worker, especially one doing manual or skilled tasks.

clue.text: Improving English and longing to ring one female

indicators.note: to ring is to encircle, so the longing word surrounds the other letters

parts.note: dying for something means longing for it
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An Englishman, yearning to phone a woman, is improving himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to ring' looks like phoning but means encircle: DYING goes round I and F.
explanation.definitionFit: Edifying means morally or intellectually uplifting, so it is improving.

clue.text: Carry out desire for senior member

parts.note: to do a task is to carry it out
a yen is a longing or desire

explanation.surface: A command to act on a wish, for the sake of an elder colleague.
explanation.definitionFit: A doyen is the most respected or senior person in a group.

clue.text: Sun to rise on river? That's normal

indicators.note: in a down answer rising means the letters read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: to sun yourself is to tan
the Ural is a river in Russia and Kazakhstan

explanation.surface: Watching the sun come up over a river is the most ordinary thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sun' is a verb here, to bask, not the star.
explanation.definitionFit: Natural and normal both mean ordinary, as expected.

clue.text: Ambition to swallow stout grew

indicators.note: to swallow means the ambition word takes the other in

parts.note: an end is an aim or ambition
stout means fat or large

explanation.surface: An urge to gulp down dark beer increased.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stout' looks like the beer but means fat.
explanation.definitionFit: Enlarged as a past tense means became bigger, as grew does.

clue.text: Royal Engineers with shop to repair

parts.note: RE is the abbreviation for the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
a store is a shop

explanation.surface: Army engineers come to a shop to fix things.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore something is to mend it or return it to good condition.

clue.text: Acknowledge what one could do to hair

definitions.meaning: to acknowledge or allow that something is so, as in granting a point

definitions.text: what one could do to hair

explanation.definitionFit: To permit is to allow or concede, as acknowledging a point does; split in two it says to put waves into hair.

clue.text: Make smooth, milky coffee after following note

indicators.note: after means the coffee comes behind the abbreviation for following

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
a latte is espresso with lots of steamed milk

explanation.surface: A barista smooths a latte after hearing a note.
explanation.definitionFit: To flatten is to make level or even, removing bumps.

clue.text: Change voice briefly in front of the Queen

indicators.note: briefly means the voice word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: alto is a singing voice
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A singer modulates their voice for a moment before the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina; 'in front of' is a link placing one piece above the other.
explanation.definitionFit: To alter is to change or modify something.

clue.text: Wise man following dad's route

indicators.note: following means the wise man comes after the word for dad's

parts.note: pa is dad, so dad's gives pa's
a sage is a wise man

explanation.surface: A guru walks behind a father along his path.
explanation.definitionFit: A passage is a way through, a route or corridor.

clue.text: Physical training outside university feasible for don

indicators.note: outside means the training letters sit around the university letter

parts.note: PT is physical training
on means possible or feasible, as in that's not on

explanation.surface: PE classes outside college are workable for an academic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'don' looks like a university lecturer but is the verb to put on clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: To don a garment is to put it on, a phrasal verb.

clue.text: Government interference affected investment in Rio

indicators.note: affected means altered or acted upon, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: State meddling upset investment in a Brazilian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affected' rearranges INVESTMENT IN RIO.
explanation.definitionFit: Interventionism is the policy of the state stepping into economic or foreign affairs.

clue.text: Mix up clothing, porter possibly going topless

parts.note: garb is clothing

indicators.note: going topless means the beer word loses its first letter

parts.note: porter is a dark beer, an example of ale

explanation.surface: A railway porter muddles his uniform and strips to the waist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'porter' suggests a baggage handler but is a beer: ALE loses A to give LE.
explanation.definitionFit: To garble a message is to jumble or confuse it.

clue.text: Borrowers usually pay this attention

definitions.meaning: the charge a lender adds to a loan

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both the charge on borrowed money and the concern one pays to something.
